plan.title: First Trip to Japan in Spring: Route, Rail, Budget
plan.description: A practical plan for a couple's first spring trip to Japan, covering how many days to allow, a Tokyo, Kyoto and Osaka route, and how rail passes work now. It also explains cherry blossom timing, a realistic budget range and the etiquette that matters most.

beats.narration: Petals drift over a quiet canal in Kyoto. Hours earlier, a Tokyo station hums at dawn. Picture both on one trip. Here is how to shape it, starting with the philosopher's path in bloom and the commuters in Tokyo.

props.alt: Kyoto blossoms and a Tokyo station at dawn

beats.chapter: Shaping your route and trip length

beats.narration: How long do you need? Seven days covers the core cities, with one day trip at most. Ten days leaves room for Nara or Hakone. Fourteen days lets you add Hiroshima or Kanazawa.

props.heading: How many days?
items: 7 days: core cities, one day trip at most
10 days: room for Nara or Hakone

beats.narration: Most couples land on ten to fourteen days. Those extra days buy day trips: Nara with its deer, Hakone with Lake Ashi and Mount Fuji views, or Miyajima and its floating gate on a longer trip.
Go in order: Tokyo, then Kyoto, then Osaka. Fly into Tokyo and out of Osaka on an open-jaw ticket, so you never backtrack.

props.title: One-way route
props.caption: Fly in to Tokyo, out of Osaka

beats.narration: For nine nights, try four in Tokyo, three in Kyoto, and two in Osaka. Go lightly on arrival day, and keep a spare day for Nara or Hakone.
The Nozomi bullet train takes about two hours fifteen minutes from Tokyo to Kyoto, with a train every ten to fifteen minutes. Kyoto makes a good base: Osaka and Nara are both an easy hop away.

Cherry blossoms first. Tokyo's best viewing is usually late March into early April. Kyoto and Osaka follow within days. Picture Ueno Park, then Kyoto's Philosopher's Path, then Osaka Castle, all in pink.

beats.narration: In 2026, the best viewing was forecast as March 28 to April 4 in Tokyo, March 29 to April 5 in Kyoto, and April 1 to 7 in Osaka.
Full bloom lasts only about a week, and wind or rain can shorten it. Forecasts shift every year, so check the Japan Meteorological Corporation or Japan Meteorological Agency before booking anything.

props.text: Full bloom lasts about a week, so check the forecast before you book.

beats.narration: Now the trains. The Japan Rail Pass rose in price in October 2023, and another increase was announced for October 1, 2026. Today, a seven-day adult pass is listed at fifty thousand yen, rising to fifty-three thousand.

props.title: Now the trains. The Japan Rail Pass rose in

beats.narration: For Tokyo, Kyoto and Osaka, it rarely pays off. The pass does not cover the fast Nozomi. Pass holders must add a supplement of about 4,960 yen for Tokyo to Kyoto.

props.verdict: On this route, single tickets usually win

beats.narration: So buy individual Shinkansen tickets, consider a regional pass if you leave the main route, and load a Suica or ICOCA card for local trains, subways and buses.
One more spring pressure: Golden Week, from late April to early May, fills trains and hotels. Book your rooms early, and aim for the blossoms before that rush.

props.alt: busy commuters at a railway station

beats.narration: Here is the honest part: spring costs more. Blossom season fills Kyoto hotels fast, and prices climb with demand. Your yen budget also moves with the exchange rate, so check it before you book.

props.alt: busy pedestrians in a city in spring

beats.chapter: What it costs and how to behave

beats.narration: Plan your budget in four buckets for two people: lodging, food, transport and sights. Lodging is the swing factor. Rail is the one line you can price exactly, so start there.
Two current numbers matter. The 7-day ordinary rail pass rose to 53,000 yen on October first, about 335 dollars. And Kyoto's lodging tax reaches 10,000 yen a night for luxury ryokan.

props.label: 7-day Ordinary JR Pass since 1 Oct 2026, about $335

beats.narration: Now manners, starting on trains. Keep your phone on silent. Take no calls on board. Talk quietly, if at all. And queue at the marked spots on the platform.
Off the train, a few habits help. Take your shoes off indoors. Do not tip; it is not expected. And in many places, finish your snack before walking on.
At an onsen, wash thoroughly before you enter the bath. Tattoos can be a problem, and some baths refuse them, so check the rules before you go.
So, the takeaway. Book early, especially Kyoto hotels in blossom season. Keep the route simple: Tokyo, Kyoto, Osaka. And respect local customs. Do that, and your first trip to Japan will go smoothly.

props.text: Book early. Keep the route simple. Respect local customs.

mismatch_scenes: beat 1 (gallery): its narration never says ['Tokyo station early morning commuters', "Philosopher's Path cherry blossoms Kyoto"]

accuracy.reason: The stat scene says the pass 'rose to 53,000 yen on October first' as if it already happened, while the notes only say the rise applies to purchases from Oct 1, 2026. The Kyoto lodging tax claim is not in the notes and is stated shakily, and the budget gives no figures.

coverage.reason: Itinerary, sakura and rail are covered. The budget has no daily or total range at all, which was an explicit request. Etiquette is generic and the 2026 sakura dates are stale for a viewer in late 2026.

structure.reason: The order is logical, with chapters for route, blossoms and rail, then cost and etiquette. It is weakened by the budget section, which names buckets and delivers nothing, and by the redundant trip-length and nine-night material.

hook_ending.reason: The opening is atmospheric but just says 'picture both on one trip'. The ending is a plain recap of three points.

tone.reason: Friendly and appropriate for beginner couples, with clear short sentences.

visuals.reason: Scene types vary. But a pie chart is used for invented night splits, the title scene text is truncated ('The Japan Rail Pass rose in'), and the checklist leaves one item unchecked without reason.

originality.reason: Mostly standard travel-blog advice. There are few surprising specifics beyond the Nozomi supplement and the sakura reservation detail.

instructions.reason: No budget range was given, and the 2026 blossom dates are outdated for a viewer today (Nov 2026). The dated pass price and the 4-minute length are fine.

language.reason: Fluent and natural, with minor awkwardness such as 'starting with the philosopher's path in bloom and the commuters in Tokyo'.

defects.quote: Plan your budget in four buckets for two people: lodging, food, transport and sights.
defects.issue: No yen or dollar figures for a daily or total budget range, which the request explicitly asked for.

defects.quote: The 7-day ordinary rail pass rose to 53,000 yen on October first, about 335 dollars.
defects.issue: The script treats the rise as already in effect and attaches an unsourced exchange rate. Beat 10 says the pass is 'listed at fifty thousand yen, rising to fifty-three thousand', which contradicts this.

defects.quote: Kyoto's lodging tax reaches 10,000 yen a night for luxury ryokan.
defects.issue: The claim is not in the notes and is dated and imprecise. The tax is tiered, and the top rate applies to the most expensive rooms generally, not only ryokan.

defects.quote: In 2026, the best viewing was forecast as March 28 to April 4 in Tokyo
defects.issue: It gives a past year's forecast, with no guidance for planning 2027 beyond a generic range.

defects.quote: Now the trains. The Japan Rail Pass rose in
defects.issue: The title text is cut off mid-sentence on screen.

defects.quote: Fly into Tokyo and out of Osaka on an open-jaw ticket, so you never backtrack.
defects.issue: The pie chart for 'Nine nights' (4/3/2) is invented, and 'Go lightly on arrival day, and keep a spare day' contradicts the nine-night split.

defects.quote: Most couples land on ten to fourteen days.
defects.issue: No clear recommendation, and the beats list 7/10/14 days and then plan nine nights.

defects.quote: Pass holders must add a supplement of about 4,960 yen for Tokyo to Kyoto.
defects.issue: It does not give the single-ticket fare for comparison, so the claim that single tickets win is unquantified.

wrong_facts: The 53,000 yen pass price is presented as already in effect; per the notes it applies to purchases from Oct 1, 2026, so by the video's date this is plausible, but the script contradicts itself.
Kyoto lodging tax 10,000 yen for luxury ryokan: unsourced and imprecise.
judge.summary: A tidy and friendly itinerary and rail section, but it skips the requested budget range entirely and contains a self-contradictory pass price and an unsourced lodging-tax claim. The coverage of blossoms relies on the past 2026 forecast and the etiquette is generic.
